A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboMD, with matching authors, core framework, experiments and retained appendix analyses despite the changed title. All 17 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3 were readable through text extraction and rendered figures, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation and UR5e experiments, failure-ranking accuracies, embedding ablations and policy fine-tuning results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds CNN/ResNet comparisons, SO101 embedding evaluations, lighting-continuity measurements and fine-tuning comparisons.

M1.justification: Both retain PPO, the ViT/CLIP embedding, nearest-known-embedding lookup and the continuous reward in Eq. 2. However, v3 defines embedding states and rewrites Algorithm 1 around virtual transitions, whereas v2 Algorithm 2 explicitly executes the manipulation policy despite prose already describing rollout-free training. This inconsistency prevents reliably distinguishing a procedural change from clarification. BCE was already documented in v2's ablations.

E1.justification: The RoboSuite/RoboMimic/MimicGen tasks and UR5e setting are retained. v3 adds real-world SO101 data for embedding evaluation (Table 6) and a graded lighting-intensity scenario (Table 7 and Figure 10). These provide limited extensions of embodiment and input-condition coverage within robot manipulation; specific SO101 tasks are not documented.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds trained CNN and reduced-channel ResNet-18 failure predictors alongside the retained RL and VLM comparators, with further results in Appendix B. This introduces a substantive comparator family testing whether lightweight supervised visual models suffice. The additional manipulation policies diagnosed by RoboMD are target policies, not new competing diagnostic methods.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce CNN/ResNet training for 200 epochs on normalized 84×84 images, a five-demonstration lighting sweep, separation/silhouette/Davies–Bouldin metrics, and fine-tuning comparisons across specified data budgets with additional error metrics (Appendix B; Tables 5–7 and 13). These substantially extend evaluation protocols without establishing changes to the retained benchmark experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds success/failure cluster-separation and lighting-continuity analyses, lightweight-detector confusion matrices, and failure-selection/data-budget comparisons. These test additional questions about embedding structure, detector errors and adaptation efficiency. v2's loss/backbone ablations, kNN analysis, training-loss curves and color-based fine-tuning analyses remain, sometimes relocated or combined.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.3 adds descriptive correlation estimation for the lighting sweep, reporting Kendall's tau of 1.000 and Pearson's r of 0.982. Neither version provides empirical seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The confidence-band discussion in v3 Appendix A concerns theoretical assumptions.

E6.justification: Matched scores in v2 Tables I, III, IV and V remain unchanged in v3 Tables 1, 2, 3 and 9. Substantial new entries cover lightweight detectors, additional target policies, embedding diagnostics and fine-tuning, including 92.83% accuracy with RoboMD-selected failures versus 85.48% with all failures (Table 13). Additionally, Milk Carton/Sprite likelihoods change from 23.2/20.2 in v2 Figure 7 to 20.2/23.2 in v3 Figure 6, reversing their displayed order.

T1.justification: v2 provides mathematical formulations but no comparable theorem-and-proof development. v3 Section 3.5 and Appendix A introduce potential-based optimality and advantage invariance, boundary-exploration sample complexity, and critic-convergence claims with proofs and lemmas. New assumptions include Lipschitz continuity, classifier calibration, boundary regularity and a Gaussian-process surrogate.

C1.justification: v3 elevates semantic potential fields and theoretical guarantees into central contributions, supplementing v2's empirical diagnosis and policy-improvement claims. It also foregrounds safe virtual evaluation and improved performance with much less fine-tuning data. Its abstract describes the approximately 23% advantage as additional unique vulnerabilities, whereas the corresponding retained benchmark reports pairwise ranking accuracy.

C2.justification: v3 adds potential-field and semantic-smoothness explanations, attributes differing policy weaknesses to inductive biases, and interprets lightweight-model results as evidence of inadequate sensitivity to subtle failures. It newly acknowledges physically unrealizable embedding states. v2's explicit concluding warning about declining performance far from known environments disappears, although distance-based uncertainty discussion remains.

D1.justification: v3 discloses computing resources, approximately 12-hour training, software and precision settings, exact ViT/CLIP variants and weights, joint encoder fine-tuning, and k=5. It newly specifies 500 benchmark pairs and supplies a repository address and reproducibility statement. This does not establish expansion of v2's separate 100-pair unseen evaluation. Conversely, that unseen-pair count and v2's indexed 21-action Lift specification are omitted.

R1.justification: Most failure-diagnosis and generalization positioning is retained. v3 adds Ng et al. (1999) for reward shaping, Gotovos et al. (2013) for level-set estimation, and recent VLA and failure-detection references, alongside Appendix B's taxonomy. References to Thrun (2002), Wilson et al.'s SAFE and Kirchheim et al.'s PyTorch-OOD are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. v3 organizes the narrative around two diagnostic challenges and continuous semantic search, making discrete search a special case. It adds dedicated theory, ethics and reproducibility sections and substantially reorganizes the appendices.

P2.justification: The two-column document becomes a single-column ICLR layout. Framework diagrams are redrawn, policy radar plots are combined and expanded, and the fine-tuning radar gains comparison curves and data-cost annotations. New tables and continuity/baseline figures accompany extensive regrouping and relocation; v2's separate kNN and training-loss plots become v3 Figure 16.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful comparator coverage, embedding checks, fine-tuning evidence and implementation information. However, its new central guarantees are not established for the reported Eq. 2 reward: the proofs invoke different shaping and uncertainty-bonus formulations without demonstrating equivalence. Appendix A's convergence proof also incorrectly infers strictly earlier convergence from smaller error upper bounds. These substantial empirical and documentation benefits coexist with new correctness problems, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
